text:
The mind—composed of organic neurons—will not say the same words every time to the same question.

An AI base model, however, will give the same output to the same input every time.

That’s why AI companies put in random number generators. Calling this consciousness is stupid. https://t.co/6xlUR1aaYq

quoted.text: You can calculate how a clump of neurons will react to electrical impulses by hand. It’s a math problem. Clearly a large clump of neurons can’t be conscious!! https://t.co/pK5cEztD89

text:
The below is not accurate. An artificial neural network is deterministic, not arbitrary. It generates the same output to the same input every time. Because it’s math.

What makes AI models arbitrary is that AI companies stick in random number generators. That’s not consciousness. https://t.co/NKVrNWvR6a

quoted.text:
No. A concatenation of many matrix multiplications is… just a single matrix multiplication (that’s what linearity means).

Rather, a neural network is a concatenation of matrix multiplications *and* nonlinearities, i.e. a concatenation of arbitrary linear and nonlinear operations, i.e. an arbitrary operation.

So the relevant question is rather: can consciousness be instantiated by an arbitrary abstract operation?
I’d say it’s pretty clear which way round the burden of proof goes.
